_comment: The canonical protect-main ruleset. One definition; apply.sh merges each repo's
own required status checks over `required_status_checks`, the only field that
legitimately differs between consumers. Everything else is shared, and a
difference is drift rather than configuration.
There is deliberately NO copilot_code_review rule. That rule makes Copilot review
automatically -- on every PR when it opens, and on every push with review_on_push --
which is how a four-push PR collected five reviews and hit the account rate limit
(tinbee/foliot#15, 2026-09-29). Copilot reviews only when asked: add the
`copilot-review` label and copilot-review.yml requests it, the same shape as
claude-review. By hand that is:
gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/pulls/N/requested_reviewers -X POST \
-f 'reviewers[]=copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]'
The [bot] suffix is required -- without it the API answers 422 'Reviews may only
be requested from collaborators', which makes it look impossible. Verified on
foliot#15. requested_reviewers reads empty straight afterwards because Copilot
consumes the request rather than queueing it, so a new review appearing is the
only confirmation.
pull_request.required_review_thread_resolution is TRUE, and it is what actually
prevents a merge over open findings: both review bots submit as COMMENTED, so
reviewDecision stays clean however many threads are unresolved.
GitHub ignores unknown members, so this key is inert.
./rulesets/apply.sh <owner/repo> [extra-check ...]
./rulesets/apply.sh --check <owner/repo> [extra-check ...]
name: protect-main
_comment_ref_name: refs/heads/main, not ~DEFAULT_BRANCH, because that is what all three consumers
actually have. ~DEFAULT_BRANCH is the more robust spelling and would survive a
default-branch rename, but adopting it here would make every repo report drift on
the first check -- which is how a guard gets ignored. Switch all three together,
